title: Condensate Drainpipe Flood & Flow Test Record
source: spec/Condensate_Drainpipe_Flood_and_Flow_Test.html (MOS-ACMV-006 — Condensate Drainpipe Flood & Flow Test Record). **Rev B replaces Rev A outright.** Rev A was the 2012 sanitary-style flood sheet retitled for condensate runs; this Rev B is a different form written against the method statement: Part A is the flood test with numbered readings and their requirements (Clause 6.2), Part B is a per-AHU flow test with a recovery percentage (Clause 6.3), and the sign-off roles change to Tested / Witnessed / Verified. Rev A is NOT bundled alongside: production D1 held no CPF@A record on 20 Sep 2026 (`SELECT … WHERE template_version_id LIKE 'CPF%'` returned nothing), so there is no filed record for a frozen Rev A to serve, and git history keeps its definition. This is the opposite call from `inspection-request-form.json`, where two IRF@A drafts existed and Rev A therefore stays bundled (SPEC §2, §12). The supplied file was saved with a project's own values in it (AMK1 UPS System C, its Location and Test Area) — those are record values and are not carried here; only Contractor and MOS Reference are defaults, because they are the same on every copy of this form.

sections.title: General Information
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is the library's grouping idiom: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same as `grease-separator-leak-test.json` and `billi-tap-test.json`.

The paper's project block (Project / Contractor / MOS Reference, beside the logo) is the record header; this section is the general-information grid beneath the title, six cells in the paper's reading order. Project carries `source: "project.name"` so it populates from record context if and when that wiring lands, but is NOT `readonly` — nothing populates `source` today, and a readonly cell with no source prints blank (the trap `meter-verification-record.json` pins in its parity test).

Test Section Length is a `number` with the unit as a field property, never written into the label (CLAUDE.md conventions); the paper writes "(m)" into its label and the renderer appends it here.

sections.title: PART A – CONDENSATE DRAIN PIPE FLOOD TEST (MOS-ACMV-006, Clause 6.2)
sections._note:
The paper's Part A table has four columns: Item, Description, Reading / Record, Requirement. The Requirement column is TEMPLATE text ("≥ 1.0 m", "≥ 30 min", "≥ 2 h", "No drop", "No") and a standard row's fourth column is the engineer's remarks cell, so each requirement is carried at the end of its description in the same words the paper prints, and the row's `limit` makes the app judge the reading the way the source's screen-only ✓/✗ indicator does. The fourth column is then a real Remarks cell — one the paper does not have, but which every standard section prints regardless.

A3 and A5 are one row each on the paper (Date: … Time: …); a checklist row carries a single control, so each is split into a dated row and a timed continuation row — the same split Rev A made, and `grease-separator-leak-test.json` cites (Hard Rule #4).

**A6 (duration) and A8 (level drop) are TYPED, not calculated.** The source computes them in its script (A5 − A3; A4 − A7). `formula` on a standard row is not evaluated by the renderer — `calculated` is a dynamic-table column type only (SPEC §12), the call `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json` records for its `max_leakage` row. The engineer reads them off, as on the printed paper. Their `limit`s still apply to what is typed.

A9 is the one question whose good answer is No, so YES maps to `fail` and NO to `pass` — read the other way round, a leaking run would drop off the outstanding-items list (SPEC §6).

rows.description: Test head above highest point of test section — requirement ≥ 1.0 m
Settlement period (release of trapped air / absorption) — requirement ≥ 30 min
Water level at commencement of test (mark on standpipe)
Water level at end of test
Drop in water level (A4 – A7) — requirement: no drop
Visible leakage at joints / fittings — requirement: No
rows._note: Yes is the failing answer here, unlike every other reading in Part A.

sections.title: PART B – CONDENSATE DRAIN PIPE FLOW TEST (MOS-ACMV-006, Clause 6.3)
sections._note:
The paper's Part B, one row per AHU: five rows drawn (`ROWS = 5` in its script), each seeded with 1.5 L poured — `prefilled_rows` carries that seed for the five the paper draws, and `carry_down` on the column copies it into any row the engineer appends, which is what the source's default `value="1.5"` does on every generated row.

**Recovery is the one figure this template DOES compute.** `calculated`, `collected / poured * 100` to one decimal — both inputs are columns of the same row, which is the scope `lib/formula.ts` resolves — A5 − A3 and A4 − A7 in Part A cannot be done the same way because a standard row has no formula evaluation.

`limit: { min: 90 }` on Recovery is the paper's acceptance figure and is DECLARATIVE today: the on-screen computed cell prints the figure without a verdict, and `lib/outstanding.ts` evaluates limits on standard number rows and matrix bands only, never on a dynamic-table column. The source's script colours its `rec` cell red below 90%; the engineer reads the printed percentage against the criteria line instead, and records P / F in the Result column, which IS evaluated (a `status` outcome). Making the computed cell judge itself is renderer code, not a template edit.

The two choice columns keep the paper's own words: Yes / No for free flow, and P / F for the result. Yes and P are the passing answers.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria (MOS-ACMV-006, Section 7) — Flood test: no visible leakage and no drop in water level over the 2-hour test period. Flow test: volume collected ≥ 90% of volume poured (≥ 1.35 L for 1.5 L); water drains freely with no ponding, backflow or leakage.
sections._note:
Two boxes on the paper, one section here. The first box is the acceptance-criteria prose; the schema has no free-text block, so the two sentences are carried in this section's `title` — the idiom `grease-separator-leak-test.json` uses for its certification sentence — because they are what the PASS / FAIL cells above are judged against and the printed sheet must show them. The second box (Instruments Used, Remarks, the two Attachments checkboxes) is the block directly beneath, and its four cells are this section's fields, so the criteria print as the heading of the box they sit above on the paper.

The attachments are `checkbox` fields, as on `grease-separator-leak-test.json`, and sit above the sign-off, never below it — what a signature covers must be settled above it.

Instruments Used stays free text: the paper draws one ruled line, not a calibration table, so no `instruments` block is declared and `link_to_instrument_register` has nothing to read.

fields.label: Attachment — Photo record (start / end level, water collected)

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note:
An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, and the paper closes its single sheet with the signature rows directly beneath the remarks box. Both carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. No `page_break_before` — it shares the Part B page.

The paper's role cells are two lines each: the role in bold and the organisation in italics beneath. "(Kenyon)" is the locked company default on the Tested By slot. "(T&C Consultant – NDR)" names a project's consultant — NDR is a record value, not template wording — so the role keeps the generic half and the signer supplies the company. "(Client, if any)" is carried verbatim in the role: it is the paper's own note that the slot may go unsigned, which is why `required` is false and why `client` is the stage — an unsigned optional slot still gates accepted, but only because someone must accept.
